It's important to emphasis that **Huckel's** [MOT]{#Blk} is based on several bold assumptions (**Eqn. 51**). Besides dealing with only $\large \pi$-electrons, it also makes a number of important assumptions about the calculus used to describe the energy of a [MO]{#Blk}, namely the <b>Coulombic</b> ($\text H_{i,j}$, for $i = j$), <b>Overlap</b> ($\text S_{i,j}$, for $i \ne j$), and <b>Resonance</b> ($\text H_{i,j}$, for $i \ne j$) integrals.  


$$\tag{51}$$


$$\text{Huckel MO assumptions:}
\\
\Big[ \text{Note: semi-emperical method relies on experimental inputs} \Big]
\\
\begin{align*}
\large 1. & \normalsize \phantom{.} \text{Applies only to} \; \large \pi \normalsize \; \text{electron systems}
\\
\large 2. & \normalsize \phantom{.} \text{Integral values }
\left[
\begin{array}{l}
\text{Coulombic:} \phantom{.} \text H_{ij} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \phantom{...} (\text{when } i = j, \, \text{emperical variable})
\\
\text{Resonance:} \phantom{.} \text H_{ij} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \beta \phantom{...} (\text{when } i \ne j, \, \text{emperical variable})
\\
\text{Resonance:} \phantom{.} \text H_{ij} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{...} (\text{when } i \ne j, \, \text{non-bonded atoms})
\\
\text{Overlap:} \phantom{.} \text S_{ij} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{...} (\text{when} \phantom{.} i = j)
\\
\text{Overlap:} \phantom{.} \text S_{ij} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{...} (\text{when} \phantom{.} i \ne j)
\\ \end{array} \right.
\\
\end{align*}$$


The **Coulombic integral** ($\large \alpha$) describes the binding energy of a $\large \pi$-electron within an [AO]{#Blk}. In other words it's the amount of energy required to remove an electron from the orbital and place it far from the nucleus where its potential energy would be zero (i.e. Vacuum level &rarr; $\text E_{\infty} = 0$). As a consequence the value of $\large \alpha$ is always negative. The **Exchange** or **Resonance Integral** ($\large \beta$) describes the energy of a $\large \pi$-electron within a multi-nuclei field. It's essentially a measure of the bond strength between two atoms, which increases with increasing [AO]{#Blk} overlap. So when the **Overlap Integral** ($\text S$) is zero then $\large \beta$ must also be zero. Lastly the **Overlap Integral** ($\text S$), as the name suggests, describes the degree of physical overlap between bonding orbitals, such as two adjacent [2]{#Blk}[&pscr;<sub>z</sub>]{#Blue} [AO]{#Blk}. The nature of the integrals is largely explained by **Eqn. 29**, with each mapping to distinct spatial regions. The **Coulombic Integral** maps the long-range electrostatic repulsion or attraction between charge densities (e.g. $\big(\text{a}_1 \, \text{2s} \big)^2$ and $\big( \text{b}_1 \, \text{2p}_z \big)^2$). The **Resonance** or **Exchange Integral** ($\large \beta$), as the name suggests, describes <u>non-classical</u> interactions within the shared inter-orbital region (i.e. $2 \text{a}_1 \text{b}_1 \big( \text{2s} \, \text{2p}_z \big)$). It is literally where electrons can be <u>exchanged</u> between orbitals. Lastly the **Overlap Integral** ($\text S$) physically maps to the inter-nuclear region where the atomic wave functions either positively or negatively interact with each other (i.e. $2 \text{a}_1 \text{b}_1 \big( \text{2s} \, \text{2p}_z \big)$), which determines the extent of covalent bonding (e.g. constructive interference = overlapping [AO]{#Blk} are <u>in phase</u>).  
&nbsp; &nbsp; The above mathematical treatment is only made possible by another important assumption known as the **Born-Oppenheimer Approximation** (**BOA**).<b>[@born_zur_1927]</b> Based on the differences in the mass of the electron and nucleus ($m_p / m_e \approx 1836$), it's possible to assume that the motion of the nucleus is relatively static when compared to the motion of an electron. Fixing the nuclear geometry (i.e. ignoring the kinetic energy contribution of the nucleus) greatly simplifies the integral energy calculations for [MO]{#Blk} (i.e. fewer &ldquo;<i>moving bodies</i>&rdquo;). This is somewhat analogous to the movement of the planets in relation to the sun. Most people typically view the sun as a fixed object that governs planetary motions. However, the sun does in fact revolve around the centre of the Milky Way,<b>[@oort_observational_1927]</b> which is ~27,000 **l**ight **y**ears away (i.e. 1 **ly** is ~9.5 &times; 10<sup>15</sup> m), at ~220 km/sec.<b>[@kerr_review_1986]</b> According to **Newtonian** mechanics (Time = $\text{d}/\vec v = (2 \large \pi \normalsize \, \text r)/\vec v$) this would mean the sun completes one rotation every ~232 million earth years. However, by assuming the sun does not move in relation to our orbiting planet is a reasonable hypothesis, certainly one that helped <b><a class="one" href="https://www.space.com/15684-nicolaus-copernicus.html" target="_blank" title="Go to Space.com">Nicolaus Copernicus</a></b> (1543) revolutionize our understanding of the universe.<b>[@copernicus_nicolai_1543]</b> So assuming a fixed nuclear configuration at any given instant in time simplifies the wave equations ($\hat H \, \psi_{\text o} = \text E \, \psi_{\text o}$) used to describe orbital electrons within a multi-nuclei potential energy field.  


$$\\
\large \text{Hamiltonian Energy Relationship} 
\\
\Big[ \, \hat H \, = \, \text{Hamiltonian operator}, \; V \, = \, \text{Potential Energy}, \; \large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize = \text{trial MO wave function} \Big]
\\
\text E \cdot \large \psi \normalsize (x) \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \overbrace{\Bigg( \frac{- \hbar^2}{2m} \cdot \frac{\partial^2}{\partial x^2} \; + \; V (x) \Bigg)}^{\large \hat H} \cdot \large \psi \normalsize (x) \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} \text E_{\pi} \cdot \large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \hat H \cdot \large \psi_{\pi}
\\
\\[10px]
\text{Multiple by } \large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \text{ then integrate and solve for } \text E_{\pi}
\\[10px]
\int \large \psi^*_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} \text E_{\pi} \phantom{.} \large \psi^{\phantom{.}}_{\pi} \normalsize \, d \text v \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \int \large \psi^*_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} \hat H \normalsize \phantom{.} \large \psi^{\phantom{.}}_{\pi} \normalsize \, d \text v \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} \overbrace{\text E_{\pi}}^{\text{constant}} \cdot \int \large \psi^*_{\pi} \psi^{\phantom{.}}_{\pi} \normalsize \, d \text v \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \int \large \psi^*_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} \hat H \phantom{.} \large \psi^{\phantom{.}}_{\pi} \normalsize \, d \text v 
\\
\large \text E_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{\int \large \psi^*_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} \hat H \phantom{.} \large \psi^{\phantom{.}}_{\pi} \normalsize \, d \text v}{\int \large \psi^*_{\pi} \; \psi^{\phantom{.}}_{\pi} \normalsize \, d \text v} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \overbrace{\frac{\langle \large \psi^*_{\pi} \normalsize \; | \hat H | \; \large \psi^{\phantom{.}}_{\pi} \normalsize \rangle}{\langle \large \psi^*_{\pi} \normalsize \; | \; \large \psi^{\phantom{.}}_{\pi} \normalsize \rangle}}^{\large {\text{Dirac's simplified} \\ \text{Bra-Ket Notation}}}
\\[40px]
\text{LCAO:} \; \large \pi \normalsize \text{-electron system where} \; \large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \, = \, \text{ MO wave function (e.g. ethylene)}
\\
\text{Let} \; \large \phi \normalsize = \text{ 2p}_z \text{ AO wave function}
\\
\large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2}
\\
\begin{align*}
\\
\large \text E_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} \frac{\int \big( c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2} \normalsize \big) \phantom{.} \hat H \phantom{.} \big( c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2} \normalsize \big) \phantom{.} d \text v}{\int \big( c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2} \normalsize \big)^2 \, d \text v}
\\
\large \text{E}_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} \frac{\int \Big( c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \hat H c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \; + \; c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \hat H c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2} \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2} \normalsize \hat H c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2} \normalsize \hat H c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2} \normalsize \Big) d \text v}{\int \big( c_1 \large \phi_{\normalsize 1} \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_{\normalsize 2} \normalsize \big)^2 \phantom{.} d \text v}
\\
\end{align*}$$


$$\text{Simplify expression using following terms:}
\\
\text{Overlap Integral} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \int \large \phi_i \phi_j \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \text S_{ij} \phantom{..} \text{when: } i \ne j
\\
\text{Coulombic Integral} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.}  \int \large \phi_i \normalsize \hat H \phi_j \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \text H_{ij} \phantom{..} \text{when: } i = j
\\
\text{Resonance Integral} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \int \large \phi_i \normalsize \hat H \large \phi_j \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \text H_{ij} \phantom{..} \text{when: } i \ne j
\\$$


Since the electronic energy of a trial wave function is always greater than or equal to the &ldquo;<i>true</i>&rdquo; ground state energy (i.e. basis of **Variational Principle**), then the best solution is to <u>minimize</u> the trial wave function with respect to each variable (i.e. coefficient). Mathematically this means setting the <b><a class="one" href="https://www.mathsisfun.com/definitions/partial-derivative.html" target="_blank" title="Go to MathIsFun">partial derivatives</a></b> to <u>zero</u> and then solving for the unknown variables (i.e. energy integrals and coefficients).  


$$\\
\text{E}_{\pi} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{c_1^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{11} + 2c_1 c_2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{12} + c_2^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{22}}{c_1^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{11} + 2c_1 c_2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{12} + c_2^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{22}}
\\
\phantom{.}
\\
\text{Minimize } \text E_{\pi} \text{ (Variational Principle)}
\\
\Big[ \text{E}_{\pi} \ge \text{E}_{\text o} \Longrightarrow \text{for best approximation minimize with respect to} \; c_1 \; \text{and} \; c_2 \Big]
\\
\frac{\partial \text E_{\pi}}{\partial c_1} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{...} \text{and} \phantom{...} \frac{\partial \text E_{\pi}}{\partial c_2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\begin{align*}
\overbrace{\text E_{\pi}}^{\text{constant}} \frac{\partial}{\partial c_1} \; \Big( c_1^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{11} \; + \; 2c_1 c_2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{12} \; + \; c_2^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{22} \Big) \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \frac{\partial}{\partial c_1} \Big( c_1^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{11} \; + \; 2c_1 c_2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{12} \; + \; c_2^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{22} \Big)
\\
\text E_{\pi} \Big( 2 c_1 \text S_{11} \; + \; 2 c_2 \text S_{12} \Big) \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} 2c_1 \text H_{11} \; + \; 2 c_2 \text H_{12}
\\
c_2 \Big( \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \; - \; \text H_{12} \Big) \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_1 \Big( \text H_{11} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{11} \Big)
\\
0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_1 \Big( \text H_{11} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{11} \Big) \; + \; c_2 \Big( \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \Big)
\\
\overbrace{\text E_{\pi}}^{\text{constant}} \frac{\partial}{\partial c_2} \phantom{.} \Big( c_1^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{11} \; + \; 2c_1 c_2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{12} \; + \; c_2^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{22} \Big) \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \frac{\partial}{\partial c_2} \Big( c_1^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{11} \; + \; 2c_1 c_2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{12} \; + \; c_2^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{22} \Big)
\\
\text E_{\pi} \Big( 2 c_1 \text S_{12} \; + \; 2 c_2 \text S_{22} \Big) \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} 2 c_1 \text H_{12} \; + \; 2 c_2 \text H_{22}
\\
c_1 \Big( \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \; - \; \text H_{12} \Big) \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_2 \Big( \text H_{22} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{22} \Big)
\\
0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_1 \Big( \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \Big) \; + \; c_2 \Big( \text H_{22} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{22} \Big)
\\
\end{align*}$$


$$\\
\begin{align*}
\\
\overbrace{ \left. \begin{array}{l}
\large 0 \normalsize \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \large c_1 \normalsize \Big( \large \text H_{11} \normalsize \phantom{.} - \phantom{.} \large \text E_{\pi} \text S_{11} \normalsize \Big) \phantom{.} + \phantom{.} \large c_2 \normalsize \Big( \large \text H_{12} \normalsize \phantom{.} - \phantom{.} \large \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \phantom{.} \Big)
\\
\large 0 \normalsize \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \large c_1 \normalsize \Big( \large \text H_{12} \normalsize \phantom{.} - \phantom{.} \large \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \normalsize \Big) \phantom{.} + \phantom{.} \large c_2 \normalsize \Big( \large \text H_{22} \normalsize \phantom{.} - \phantom{.} \large \text E_{\pi} \text S_{22} \normalsize \Big)
\\
\end{array}
\right]}^{\large \text{Homogeneous Linear Equations}} \; \large \text{Secular Equations}
\end{align*}
\\$$

 
The above **secular equations** are used to calculate the electronic energy of the [MO]{#Blk}, as well as the relative contribution that each [AO]{#Blk} makes (i.e. **coefficients**) to each [MO]{#Blk} wave function (i.e. bonding and anti-bonding [MO]{#Blk}). Since each **secular equation** is equal to zero (i.e. constant) they can also be classified as <u>homogeneous linear equations</u>. What's <u>most important</u> here is that the **coefficients** <u>must be non-zero values</u> (i.e. non-trivial solutions). As a consequence the <b><a class="one" href="https://www.mathsisfun.com/algebra/matrix-determinant.html" target="_blank" title="Go to MathIsFun">secular determinant</a></b> (i.e. bracketed terms) must be <u>equal to zero</u> in order to satisfy the mathematical expression (i.e. <b>LS = RS</b>).  


$$\\
\text{System of Equations: Solve for } c_1
\\
\big[\text{Note: for brevity the integral expressions have been assigned letters} \big]
\\
\begin{align*}
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \phantom{....} 0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} c_1 \overbrace{\Big( \text H_{11} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{11} \Big)}^{\text{X}} \; + \; c_2 \overbrace{\Big(\text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \normalsize \text S_{12} \Big)}^{\text Y}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} \phantom{.} \phantom{....} 0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} c_1 \overbrace{\Big( \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \Big)}^{\text Y} \; + \; c_2 \overbrace{\Big( \text H_{22} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{22} \Big)}^{\text Z}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \times \text Z \phantom{....} 
0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} c_1 \text{XZ} \; + \; c_2 \text{YZ} 
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} \times \text Y \phantom{....} 
0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} c_1 \text{YY} \; + \; c_2 \text{ZY}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{5} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \; - \; \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} \phantom{....} 0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} c_1 \text{XZ} \; + \; \require{cancel} \cancel{c_2 \text{ZY}} \; - \; \big( c_1 \text{YY} \; + \; \require{cancel} \cancel{c_2 \text{ZY}} \big)
\\
0 \phantom{.} = & \phantom{..} c_1 \big( \text{XZ} \; - \; \text{YY} \big)
\\
0 \phantom{.} = & \phantom{..} c_1 \overbrace{\Big[ \big( \text H_{11} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{11} \big) \big( \text H_{22} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{22} \big) \; - \; \big( \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \big) \big( \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} \big)\Big]}^{\large \text{Secular Determinant} \; (|det|)}
\\[10px]
\large |det| \normalsize \phantom{.} = & \phantom{.} \large \text{XZ} \normalsize \; - \; \large \text{YY} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \large \left| \begin{array}
\text H_{11} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{11} &
\phantom{..} \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12}
\\
\text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{12} &
\phantom{..} \text H_{22} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \text S_{22}
\end{array}
\right| \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \large 0
\end{align*}
\\$$


The 2 &times; 2 matrix block (i.e. **secular determinant**) is the product of two [2]{#Blk}[&pscr;<sub>z</sub>]{#Blue} [AO]{#Blk}. Its diagonal elements (top left to bottom right) are the **Coulombic integrals**, while the off-diagonal elements (top right to bottom left) are the **Resonance** or **Exchange integrals**.  


$$\\
\large |det| \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \left| \begin{array}
\\
\overbrace{\text H_{11}}^{\large \alpha} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \overbrace{\text S_{11}}^{\large 1} &
\phantom{..} \overbrace{\text H_{12}}^{\large \beta} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \overbrace{\text S_{12}}^{\large 0}
\\
\overbrace{\text H_{12}}^{\large \beta} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \overbrace{\text S_{12}}^{\large 0} &
\phantom{..} \overbrace{\text H_{22}}^{\large \alpha} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \overbrace{\text S_{22}}^{\large 1}
\end{array} \right| \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \overbrace{\left| \begin{array}
\\
\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\pi} & \beta
\\
\beta & \phantom{.} \alpha \; - \; \text E_{\pi}
\end{array}
\right|}^{\large \text{New Matrix}^{\dagger}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\[10px]
\big[ \phantom{.}^{\dagger} \text{Note: see list of Huckel's assumptions in Eqn. 51} \phantom{.} \big]
\\[5px]
\text{Divide each matrix element by} \, \beta \, \text{and let:} \; \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\pi}}{\beta} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} x
\\
\large |det| \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \left| \begin{array}
\\
x & \phantom{.} 1
\\
1 & \phantom{.} x
\end{array}
\right| \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\[10px]
\text{Expand Determinant}
\\
x^2 \;  - \; 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \pm \thinspace 1 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} 2 \phantom{.} \text{energy solutions}
\\[10px]
\begin{align*}
\text{when } x = -1 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow &
\phantom{..} \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\pi}}{\beta} \phantom{.} \; = \; -1 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} \text E_{\pi} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \phantom{.} + \phantom{.} \beta
\\
\text{when} \, x = 1 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow &
\phantom{..} \frac{\alpha \phantom{.} - \phantom{.} \text E_{\pi}}{\beta} \; = \; 1 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} \text E_{\pi} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; - \; \beta
\end{align*}$$


The two <u>roots</u> of the **secular determinant** provide the energy of the $\large \pi$-electrons (i.e. energy *eigenvalues*). Inputting the actual (experimental) energy values for the **Coulombic integral** (i.e. $\alpha \approx 11.4 \, e \text V$) and **Resonance integral** (i.e. $\beta \approx 0.674 \, e \text V$) of a carbon [2]{#Blk}[&pscr;<sub>z</sub>]{#Blue} [AO]{#Blk} makes it possible to properly graph the energy levels of a $\large \pi$-electron system (**Fig. 24**). Following the *Aufbau* principle the first two $\large \pi$-electrons are placed in the lowest energy level (i.e. $\text E = \alpha \normalsize \; + \; \beta$), which represents the lone $\large \pi$-<b>bonding</b> [MO]{#Blk} (Note: $\beta$ is negative since the vacuum level is zero). The total energy of the two $\large \pi$-electron system is $2(\alpha \; + \; \beta)$. To determine the values of the two coefficients (i.e. <b>c<sub>1</sub></b> and <b>c<sub>2</sub></b>) one needs to simply plug one of the energy values (e.g. $\text E_{\pi} = \alpha \; + \; \beta$) into the <b>secular equations</b> and then systematically solve for each coefficient.  


$$\text{Apply Huckel Approximations and Plug in Energy Value} \, (\alpha + \beta)
\\
\begin{align*}
0 \phantom{.} = & \phantom{..} c_1 \Big( \overbrace{\text H_{11}}^{\large \alpha} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \overbrace{\text S_{11}}^{\large 1} \Big) \; + \; c_2 \Big(\overbrace{\text H_{12}}^{\large \beta} \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \normalsize \overbrace{\text S_{12}}^{\large 0} \Big)
\\
0 \phantom{.} = & \phantom{.} c_1 \Big( \alpha \; - \; \text E_{\pi} \Big) \; + \; c_2 \beta
\\
0 \phantom{.} = & \phantom{.} c_1 \Big( \require{cancel} \cancel{\alpha} \; - \; \big[ \require{cancel} \cancel{\alpha} \; + \; \beta \big] \Big) \; + \; c_2 \beta \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} - c_1 \beta \; + \; c_2 \beta
\\
c_1 \beta \phantom{.} = & \phantom{.} c_2 \beta \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_2
\\
\end{align*}
\\[10px]
\text{Apply Normalization Conditions}
\\
\big[ \, \text{See Fig. 18} \, \big]
\\
\sum c^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1^2 \; + \; c_2^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} 2c_1^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_2
\\
\text{Normalized Density Function} \; \big( \psi_{\pi}^2 \big)
\\
\text{Since:} \phantom{..} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_2 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1 \big( \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \large \phi_2 \normalsize \big)
\\
\large \psi_{\pi}^2 \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1^2 \big( \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \large \phi_2 \normalsize \big)^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1
\\[10px]
c_1^2 \Big( \overbrace{\large \phi_1^2}^{\text S_{11} \; = \; 1} \; + \; 2 \overbrace{\large \phi_1 \, \phi_2}^{\text S_{12}^{\dagger} \; = \; 0} \; + \; \overbrace{\large \phi_2^2}^{\text S_{22} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1} \normalsize \Big) \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1
\\
\Big[ \;^{\dagger} \text{Note: see list of Huckel's assumptions} \; \Big]
\\
2c_1^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_2
\\
\large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \Big( \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \large \phi_2 \normalsize \Big)
\\$$


The energy diagram for a single $\large \pi$ bond system (i.e. **ethylene**) shows two [2]{#Blk}[&pscr;<sub>z</sub>]{#Blue} [AO]{#Blk} forming one <b>bonding</b> ($\text E_{\pi} = \alpha + \beta$) and one <b>anti-bonding</b> ($\text E_{\pi^*} = \alpha - \beta$) <b>MO</b> (Note: both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ values are < 0 <b>eV</b>, which is the energy value assigned to a free electron at rest in a perfect vacuum far removed from the nucleus).

<figure>
![](images/Ethylene_HMO_diagram.jpg){width=600px}
</figure>
</div>

<!------------------------------------------------------>
<!------------------------------------------------------>


To appreciate the significance of a conjugated $\large \pi$-bond system we need to look at how it affects the stability and reactivity of a molecule, such as the relatively simple three carbon **Allyl** system.  


$$\large \overbrace{\text R - \text C = \text C  - \overset{\Large 1}{\text C} \text H_3}^{\large \text{Simple Alkene}}
\\ 
\big[ \, \text{Allylic position} \; = \; \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} , \phantom{..} \text{Allyl} \phantom{.} \text C - \text H \phantom{.} \text{bond energy} \, \approx \, 320 \, \text{kJ/mol} \, \big]
\\[15px]
\large \overbrace{\text R^{'} - \text C = \text C  - \overset{\Large 2}{\text C} \text H_2 - \text C = \large \text C - \text R^{''}}^{\large \text{Simple Diene}}
\\ 
\big[ \, \text{Bis-allylic position} \; = \; \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} , \phantom{..} \text{Bis-allylic} \phantom{.} \text C - \text{H} \phantom{.} \text{bond energy} \approx 314 \, \text{kJ/mol} \, \big]
\\$$


In organic chemistry an <b><a class="one" href="https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/A00245" target="_blank" title="Go to IUPAC">allylic</a></b> carbon bond is known to be more prone to chemical attack than its <b><a class="one" href="https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/A00222" target="_blank" title="Go to IUPAC">alkane</a></b> (saturated) counterparts. As discussed below being next to a conjugated $\large \pi$-bond makes <b>allylic</b> bonds relatively weaker and therefore more susceptible to reactive agents like free radicals. All three <b>Allyl</b> &ldquo;<i>species</i>&rdquo; contain a $\large \pi$-bond and an **allylic** carbon either in the form of: <b>(i)</b> a carbo-<b>cation</b> (i.e. system holds 2 $\large \pi$ [[e]{#Red}]{#strokeB}<b><sup>-</sup></b>); <b>(ii)</b> a <b>radical</b> (i.e. system holds 3 $\large \pi$ [[e]{#Red}]{#strokeB}<b><sup>-</sup></b>); or <b>(iii)</b> an <b>anion</b> (i.e. system holds 4 $\large \pi$ [[e]{#Red}]{#strokeB}<b><sup>-</sup></b>). All three <b>allyl</b> &ldquo;<i>species</i>&rdquo; have three spatially aligned [2]{#Blk}[&pscr;<sub>z</sub>]{#Blue} orbitals (i.e. conjugated). The only major difference is the total number of $\large \pi$-electrons found within these three &ldquo;<i>species</i>&rdquo; (<b>Fig. 25</b>). Applying the <b>LCAO</b> method to the <b>Allyl</b> system produces three $\large \pi$ [MO]{#Blk}, namely <b>(i)</b> one <u>bonding</u> ($\large \pi_{\normalsize 1}$), <b>(ii)</b> one <u>non-bonding</u> ($\large \pi_{\normalsize 2}$), and <b>(iii)</b> one <u>anti-bonding</u> [MO]{#Blk} ($\large \pi_{\normalsize 3}$). All three [2]{#Blk}[&pscr;<sub>z</sub>]{#Blue} orbitals that make up the $\large \pi_{\normalsize 1}$ [MO]{#Blk} are in phase with one another, while the non-bonding $\large \pi_{\normalsize 2}$ and anti-bonding $\large \pi_{\normalsize 3}$ [MO]{#Blk} have one or two nodal planes, respectively, due to orbital phase shifts.

Carrying out the energy calculations for the three contiguous [2]{#Blk}[&pscr;<sub>z</sub>]{#Blue} orbitals making up the **Allyl** system produces a **determinant** in the form a 3 &times; 3 matrix block.  


$$\\
\text{Let:} \; \large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \; = \; \text{MO wave function}, \; \large \phi \normalsize \; = \; 2p_z \, \text{wave funtion}, \; c \; = \; \text{coefficient}
\\
\large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1 \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; c_3 \large \phi_3
\\[15px]
\text{Algebraic Matrices:}
\\
\text A \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} [c_1, \, c_2, \, c_3] \phantom{.....} \text B \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \left[\begin{array}
\\ \phi_1 \\ \phi_2 \\ \phi_3
\end{array}
\right]
\\
\large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \text{A} \times \text{B} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \overbrace{[c_1, \, c_2, \, c_3]
\left[\begin{array}
\\ \large \phi_1 \\ \large \phi_2 \\ \large \phi_3
\end{array}
\right]}^{\large \text{Dot Product}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1 \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; c_3 \phi_3
\\$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\text{Energy Expectation Value:}
\\
\begin{align*}
\large \text E_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \frac{\int \big( c_1 \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; c_3 \large \phi_3 \normalsize \big) \; \hat H \; \big( c_1 \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; c_3 \large \phi_3 \normalsize \big) \, d \text v}{\int \big( c_1 \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; c_3 \large \phi_3 \normalsize \big)^2 \phantom{.} d \text v}
\\
\large \text{E}_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \frac{\int \Big( c_1^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{11} \; + \; c_2^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{22} \; + \; c_3^2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{33} \; + \; 2 c_1 c_2 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{12} \; + \; 2 c_1 c_3 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{13} \; + \; 2 c_2 c_3 \text H^{\phantom{.}}_{23} \Big) d \text v}{\int \big( c_1^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{11} \; + \; c_2^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{22} \; + \; c_3^2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{33} \; + \; 2 c_1 c_2 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{12} \; + \; 2 c_1 c_3 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{13} \; + \; 2 c_2 c_3 \text S^{\phantom{.}}_{23} \big)^2 \, d \text v} \end{align*}
\\$$

<br>

$$\\
\text{Minimize} \; \text E_{\large \pi} \; \text{(Variational Principle)}
\\
\Big[ \, \text{E}_{\large \pi} \ge \text{E}_{\text o} \Longrightarrow \text{minimize with respect to} \; c_1 , \; c_2 \; \text{and} \; c_3 \, \Big]
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \phantom{.} \frac{\partial \text E_{\large \pi}}{\partial c_1} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 , \phantom{..} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} \phantom{.} \frac{\partial \text E_{\large \pi}}{\partial c_2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 , \phantom{..} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \phantom{.} \frac{\partial \text E_{\large \pi}}{\partial c_3} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\begin{align*}
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \phantom{.} \frac{\partial \text E_{\large \pi}}{\partial c_1} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_1 \Big(\text H_{11} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{11} \Big) \; + \; c_2 \Big( \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{12} \Big) \; + \; c_3 \Big( \text H_{13} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{13} \Big)
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} \phantom{.} \frac{\partial \text E_{\large \pi}}{\partial c_2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_1 \Big( \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{12} \Big) \; + \; c_2 \Big( \text H_{22} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{22} \Big) \; + \; c_3 \Big( \text H_{23} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{23} \Big)
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \phantom{.} \frac{\partial \text E_{\large \pi}}{\partial c_3} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_1 \Big( \text H_{13} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{13} \Big) \; + \; c_2 \Big( \text H_{23} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{23} \Big) \; + \; c_3 \Big( \text H_{33} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{33} \Big)
\\
\end{align*}
\\[15px]
\overbrace{\left|
\begin{array}
\\
\text H_{11} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{11} &
\phantom{..} \text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{12} &
\phantom{..} \text H_{13} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{13}
\\
\text H_{12} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{12} &
\phantom{..} \text H_{22} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{22} &
\phantom{..} \text H_{23} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{23}
\\
\text H_{13} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{13} &
\phantom{..} \text H_{23} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{23} &
\phantom{..} \text H_{33} \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi} \text S_{33}
\end{array}
\right|}^{\large |det|} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \large 0
\\
\overbrace{\left| \begin{array}
\\
\large \alpha \normalsize \; - \; \large \text E_{\pi} & \phantom{.} \large \beta & \phantom{.} \large 0
\\
\large \beta & \large \alpha \normalsize \; - \; \large \text E_{\pi} & \phantom{.} \large \beta
\\
\large 0 & \phantom{.} \large \beta & \large \alpha \normalsize \; - \; \large \text E_{\pi}
\end{array}
\right|}^{\large \text{New Matrix}^{\dagger}}
\phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \large 0
\\
\big[ \phantom{.}^{\dagger} \text{Note: see list of Huckel's assumptions} \phantom{.} \big]
\\$$


$$\\
\text{Divide elements (new matrix) by} \, \beta \, \text{and let} \, \frac{\alpha - \text E_{\pi}}{\beta} \; = \; x
\\
\large |det| \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \left| \begin{array}
\\ x & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} 0 \\ 1 & \phantom{.} x & \phantom{.} 1 \\ 0 & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} x
\end{array} \right| \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\text{Evaluate Determinant (Cofactor Expansion)}
\\
\Big[\text{Note:} \; \text C_{i, \, j} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} (-1)^{\overbrace{i \, + \, j}^{\large \text{Parity}}} \times \text M_{i, \, j} \phantom{.....} |det A|  \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} a_{1,1} \text C_{1,1} \; + \; a_{1,2} \text C_{1,2}  \; + \; a_{1,3} \text C_{1,3} \Big]
\\
\begin{align*} \left| \begin{array}
\\ x & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} 0 \\ 1 & \phantom{.} x & \phantom{.} 1 \\ 0 & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} x
\end{array}
\right| \phantom{.} = & \phantom{..} x \cdot  \overbrace{\left|
\begin{array}
\\
x & \phantom{.} 1 \\ 1 & \phantom{.} x
\end{array}
\right|}^{\large \text M_{(1,1)}} \; - \; 1 \cdot  \overbrace{\left|
\begin{array}
\\
1 & \phantom{.} 1 \\ 0 & \phantom{.} x
\end{array}
\right|}^{\large \text M_{(1,2)}} \; + \; 0 \cdot \overbrace{\left|
\begin{array}
\\
1 & \phantom{.} x \\ 0 & \phantom{.} 1
\end{array}
\right|}^{\large \text M_{(1,3)}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\[5px]
0 \phantom{.} = & \phantom{..} x \big( x^2 \, - \, 1 \big) \; - \; \big( x \, - \, 0 \big) \; + \; 0
\\[5px]
0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} x^3 \; + \; 2x \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} 3 \phantom{.} \text{roots} \phantom{.} \text{(Energy values)}
\\
\end{align*}
\\
x \phantom{..} = \phantom{..} 0 , \phantom{..} \pm \sqrt 2
\\$$


Despite the increased size of the **secular determinant** for the **Allyl** system, it still produces a relatively simple set of root values. Moreover, the calculations are <u>recursive</u> in nature since this slightly <u>larger</u> matrix (i.e. <b><i>r</i></b>ow &times; <b><i>c</i></b>olumn = 3 &times; 3) is calculated by summing **C**o-factor <u>weighted</u> <b><a class="one" href="https://mathworld.wolfram.com/DeterminantExpansionbyMinors.html" target="_blank" title="Go to MathWorld">determinants</a></b> of sub-matrices or **M**inors (<b><i>r</i></b>-1 &times; <b><i>c</i></b>-1 = 2 &times; 2 matrix), otherwise known as **Laplacian** or **Co-factor expansion**. For the first row of elements the corresponding **M**inors would be: <b>M<sub>1,1</sub></b>, <b>M<sub>1,2</sub></b>, and <b>M<sub>1,3</sub></b>. Ultimately the choice of row for making this calculation doesn't matter since they all generate the same answer (Note: row with most zeros is easier to work with). However one very important feature of the **secular determinant** formula is the <u>alternating sign</u> of the weighted **M**inors, which is due to the negative unity constant and its exponent (i.e. parity of exponent determines + or - value of the unity constant).  


$$\\
\begin{align*}
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \phantom{.} \text{when} \; x = - \sqrt 2 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi}}{\beta} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} - \sqrt 2 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_{1}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \overbrace{\alpha \; + \; \sqrt 2 \beta}^{\large \text{Bonding}}
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} \phantom{.} \text{when} \; x \, = \, 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi}}{\beta} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_{2}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \phantom{...} \text{(non-bonding level)}
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \phantom{.} \text{when} \; x = \sqrt 2 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi}}{\beta} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \sqrt 2 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_{3}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \overbrace{\alpha \; - \; \sqrt 2 \beta}^{\large \text{Anti-Bonding}}
\\
\end{align*}$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\\
\text{Secular Equation Matrix}
\\
\left| \begin{array}
\\
\; x & \; 1 & \; 0 \;
\\
\; 1 & \; x & \; 1 \;
\\
\; 0 & \; 1 & \; x \;
\end{array} \right| \; \times
\overbrace{ \left| \begin{array}
\\
\; c_1 \; \\ \; c_2 \; \\ \; c_3 \;
\end{array}
\right|}^{\text{coefficients}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{..} 0
\\
\begin{align*}
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} &
\phantom{..} c_1 \, x \; + \; c_2 \; + \; 0 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} &
\phantom{..} c_1 \; + \; c_2 \, x \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} &
\phantom{..} 0 \; + \; c_2 \; + \; c_3 \, x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \end{align*}
\\[20px]
\text{Recall: Normalization Conditions}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{\text N} \phantom{..} \large \sum c^2 \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1^2 \; + \; c_2^2 \; + \; c_3^2
\\$$


<hr style="border:1px solid gray">


$$\\
\text{when} \phantom{.} x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \phantom{..} c_1 \, (0) \; + \; c_2 \; + \; 0 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\[15px]
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} \phantom{..} c_1 \; + \; c_2 (0) \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} - \, c_3
\\[10px]
\begin{align*}
\large \sum_{i = 1}^N c^2 \normalsize \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} c_1^2 \; + \; 0 \; + \; c_3^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} 2 c_1^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1
\\
 | c_1 | \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} | c_3 | \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2}
\\[10px]
1 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} \bigg( \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2 \; + \; \bigg( \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2
\\[10px]
c_1 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} , \phantom{..} c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 , \phantom{..} c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2}
\end{align*}
\\$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\text{when} \phantom{.} x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} - \sqrt 2
\\
\begin{align*}
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \phantom{..} - c_1 \, \sqrt 2 \; + \; c_2 \; + \; 0 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_2 = \sqrt 2 \, c_1
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} \phantom{..} c_1 \; - \; \sqrt 2 \, c_2 \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \sqrt 2 \, c_2
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \phantom{..} c_2 \; - \; \sqrt 2 \, c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \sqrt 2 \, c_3
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \, \text{&} \, \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} c_2
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{\text N} \, \text{&} \, \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \bigg( \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} c_2 \bigg)^2 \; + \; c_2^2 \; + \; \bigg( \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} c_2 \bigg)^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1
\\
\end{align*}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{5} \phantom{...} 2 c_2^2 \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\pm \sqrt 2}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{5} \phantom{.} \text{&} \phantom{.} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} \phantom{...} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{2}
\\
c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{2} , \phantom{..} c_2^{\dagger} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} , \phantom{..} c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{2}
\\
\Big[ \phantom{.} ^\dagger \text{Note: since part of bonding MO = + phase} \Big]
\\$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\text{when} \phantom{.} x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \sqrt 2
\\
\begin{align*}
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \phantom{..} \sqrt 2 \, c_1 \; + \; c_2 \; + \; 0 \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_2 = - \sqrt 2 \, c_1
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} \phantom{..} c_1 \; + \; \sqrt 2 \, c_2 \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} - \sqrt 2 \, c_2
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \phantom{..} c_2 \; + \; \sqrt 2 \, c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} - \sqrt 2 \, c_3
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \, \text{&} \, \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} c_2
\\
& \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{\text N} \, \text{&} \, \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \bigg( \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} c_2 \bigg)^2 \normalsize \; + \; c_2^2 \; + \; \bigg( \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} c_2 \bigg)^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1
\\
\end{align*}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{5} \phantom{...} 2c_2^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\pm \sqrt 2}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{5} \, \text{&} \, \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} \phantom{..} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \Bigg( \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} \Bigg) c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \Bigg( \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} \Bigg) \Bigg( \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} \Bigg) \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{2}
\\
c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{2} , \phantom{..} c_2^\dagger \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} , \phantom{..} c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{2}
\\
\Big[ \phantom{.} ^\dagger \text{Note: since part of anti-bonding MO } = - \text{ phase} \Big]
\\$$


One can check the calculations above by simply plugging the energy values into the expanded energy equation as exemplified below for the bonding [MO]{#Blk} $\psi_{\pi_1}$.  


$$\\
\large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{..} \frac{1}{2} \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; \frac{1}{2} \large \phi_3 \normalsize \phantom{..} = \phantom{..} \frac{1}{2} \normalsize \Big( \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \sqrt 2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; \large \phi_3 \normalsize \Big)
\\$$


$$\\
\begin{align*}
\text E_{\pi_1} \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \Big \langle \large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \; | \hat H | \; \large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \Big \rangle \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \Bigg \langle \normalsize \frac{1}{2} \Big( \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \sqrt 2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; \large \phi_3 \normalsize \Big) \; | \hat H | \; \frac{1}{2} \Big( \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \sqrt 2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; \large \phi_3 \normalsize \Big) \Bigg \rangle
\\
= & \phantom{.} \frac{1}{4} \Bigg[ \; \overbrace{ \Big \langle \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; | \hat H | \; \large \phi_1 \normalsize \Big \rangle}^{\large \alpha \normalsize \, + \, \large \sqrt 2 \beta} \normalsize \; + \; 2 \Big( \; \sqrt 2 \; \overbrace{ \Big \langle \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; | \hat H | \; \large \phi_2 \normalsize \Big \rangle}^{\large \beta} \normalsize \; \Big) \; + \; 2 \normalsize \Big( \; \overbrace{ \Big\langle \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; | \hat H | \; \large \phi_3 \normalsize \Big \rangle}^{\large 0} \normalsize \; \Big) \; + \; 2 \Big( \, \overbrace{ \Big \langle \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; | \hat H | \; \large \phi_2 \Big \rangle}^{\large \alpha} \normalsize \; \Big)
\\
& + \phantom{.} 2 \Big( \sqrt 2 \; \overbrace{\Big \langle \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; | \hat H | \; \large \phi_3 \normalsize \Big \rangle}^{\large \beta} \normalsize \; \Big) \; + \; \overbrace{ \Big \langle \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; | \hat H | \; \large \phi_3 \normalsize \Big \rangle}^{\large \alpha \normalsize \, - \, \large \sqrt 2 \beta} \normalsize \; \Bigg]
\\
= & \frac{1}{4} \bigg[ \; \alpha \; + \; \require{cancel} \cancel{\sqrt 2 \beta} \; + \; 2 \sqrt 2 \beta \; + \; 2 \alpha \; + \; 2 \sqrt 2 \beta \; + \; \alpha \; - \; \require{cancel} \cancel{\sqrt 2 \beta} \; \bigg]
\\
= & \frac{1}{4} \bigg[ \; 4 \alpha \; + \; 4 \sqrt 2 \beta \; \bigg] \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; + \; \sqrt 2 \beta \phantom{...} \Huge \checkmark
\\
\end{align*}$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\large \text{Ethylene } \Large \pi \large \text{-electron System}
\\
\begin{align*}
& \left.
\begin{array}
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_2 \normalsize
\end{array}
\right. \Bigg\} \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_1} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; + \; \beta \phantom{..} \text{(Bonding MO)}
\\
& \left.
\begin{array}
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_2} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; - \; \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_2
\end{array}
\right. \Bigg\} \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; - \; \beta \normalsize \phantom{..} \text{(Anti-Bonding MO)}
\\
\end{align*}
\\$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\large \text{Allyl } \Large \pi \large \text{-electron System}
\\
\begin{align*}
& \left.
\begin{array}
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{2} \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; \frac{1}{2} \large \phi_3 \normalsize
\end{array}
\right. \Bigg\} \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_1} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; + \; 2 \sqrt{\beta} \phantom{..} \text{(Bonding MO)}
\\
& \left.
\begin{array}
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_2} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; (0) \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; - \; \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_3 \normalsize \end{array} \right. \Bigg\} \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \phantom{..} \text{(Non-bonded level)}
\\
& \left. \begin{array}
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_3} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{1}{2} \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; - \; \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; \frac{1}{2} \large \phi_3 \normalsize
\end{array} \right. \Bigg\} \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_3} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; - \; \sqrt{\beta} \phantom{..} \text{(Anti-Bonding MO)}
\\
\end{align*}$$



The final coefficient weighted wave functions for the **Allyl** and **Ethylene** $\large \pi$-electron systems are listed above. This information helps us understand the behaviour of <u>de-localized</u> $\large \pi$-electron systems, particularly when it is compared to a <u>localized</u> $\large \pi$-electron system depicted in <b><a class="one" href="https://lewisstructures.net/" target="_blank" title="Go to LewisStructures.net">Lewis structures</a></b> (**Fig. 22**). Based on the calculations below the so called <u>De-localization Energy</u> for the 3 $\large \pi$-electron **Allyl** system is approximately $0.83 \, \beta$.  


$$\\
\large \text{De-localization Energy:} \normalsize
\\
\Big[ \text{Note: De-localized versus localized Total } \large \pi \normalsize \text{-electron Energy} \Big]
\\
\begin{align*}
\text E_{\text{(de-localized)}} \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \text E_{\large \pi_1} \; - \; \Big( \text E_{\large \pi \normalsize (\text C_2 \text H_4)} \; + \; \alpha \Big)
\\
= & \phantom{.} \Big( \overbrace{ 2 \Big[ \alpha \; + \; \sqrt 2 \beta \Big]}^{\large \text E_{\pi_1} \; 2 \, \pi e^-} \; + \; \require{cancel} \cancel{\alpha} \Big) \; - \; \Big( \overbrace{2 \Big[ \alpha \; + \; \beta \Big]}^{\large \text E_{\pi \normalsize (\text C_2 \text H_4)} \; 2 \, \large \pi \normalsize e^-} \; + \; \require{cancel} \cancel{\alpha} \Big)
\\
= & \phantom{.} \Big( \require{cancel} \cancel{3 \alpha} \; + \; 2 \sqrt 2 \beta \Big) \; - \; \Big( \require{cancel} \cancel{3 \alpha} \; + \; 2 \beta \Big) \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 2 \sqrt 2 \beta \; - \; 2 \beta
\\
\approx & \phantom{.} 0.8284 \, \beta
\\
\end{align*}$$


The energy solutions generated by the **secular determinant** helps to explain some of the properties of the **Allyl** &ldquo;<i>species</i>&rdquo;. Of particular interest is the varying $\large \pi$-electron density and atomic charges, since they reveal potential reactive sites. For example, an atom with a partial <u>positive</u> charge will be preferentially targeted by a <b><a class="one" href="https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/N04249" target="_blank" title="Go to IUPAC">nucleophile</a></b>, whereas an atom with a partial <u>negative</u> charge will be preferentially attacked by an <b><a class="one" href="https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/E02020" target="_blank" title="Go to IUPAC">electrophile</a></b>. The <u>electronic</u> charge assigned to an atom ($j^{th}$) is simply the difference between its calculated electron density ($D_j$) and the expected electron density of a neutral one electron orbital (i.e. unity). For example, if the $j^{th}$ atom has excess electronic density ($D_j > 1$) than subtracting it from the expected value will yield a negative charge ($Q$).  


$$\\
\large \text{Allyl } \Large \pi \large \; e^- \; \text{Density}
\\
\big[ \, \text{Note: } n = \text{#}e^-, \phantom{..} \text c = \text{coefficient}, \phantom{..} k^{th} \; \text{MO}, \phantom{..} j^{th} \text{atom}, \phantom{..} Q_j = \text{atomic } e^- \text{ charge} \, \big ]
\\
\large D_{j} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \large \sum_{k \, = \, 1}^{N} n_k \; c_{k \, j}^2
\phantom{.....}
\large Q_j \normalsize \phantom{.} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \large 1 \normalsize \; - \; \large D_{j}
\\$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\large \text{Allyl Anion} \normalsize \; (4 \; \Large \pi \normalsize e^-)
\\
\begin{align*}
D_1 \normalsize \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \; + \; \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_2}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1.5 \phantom{......} Q_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 1.5 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} -0.5
\\
D_2 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \; + \; \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( 0 \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_2}} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{........} \, Q_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
D_3 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \; + \; \overbrace{ (2) \bigg(\frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_2}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1.5 \phantom{......} Q_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 1.5 \phantom{.}  = \phantom{.} -0.5
\\
\end{align*}
\\$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\large \text{Allyl Radical} \normalsize \; (3 \; \Large \pi \normalsize e^-)
\\
\begin{align*}
D_1 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \; + \; \overbrace{ (1) \bigg( \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_2}} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{......} Q_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
D_2 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \; + \; \overbrace{ (1) \bigg( 0 \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_2}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{.......} Q_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
D_3 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \large \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \; + \; \overbrace{ (1) \bigg(\frac{-1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \large \psi_{\pi_2}} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{......}
Q_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\end{align*}$$

<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\\
\large \text{Allyl Cation} \normalsize \; (2 \; \Large \pi \large e^{\normalsize -} \normalsize )
\\
\begin{align*}
D_1 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0.5 \phantom{......} Q_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 0.5 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} + 0.5
\\
D_2 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{\sqrt 2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{......}  Q_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
D_3 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \overbrace{ (2) \bigg( \frac{1}{2} \bigg)^2}^{\large i \; = \; \psi_{\pi_1}} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0.5 \phantom{......} Q_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \; - \; 0.5 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} + 0.5
\\
\end{align*}$$

Both the **anionic** and **cationic** **Allyl** &ldquo;species&rdquo; spread their respective charges evenly across the two terminal carbon atoms. This is in direct contrast to the localized electronic structure depicted in **Lewis** structures (**Fig. 25A**). The increased stability conferred by its **de-localization energy** (**DE**) is the reason why **allylic** carbon bonds are weaker than their **alkane** counterparts as exemplified by **propylene** (**Fig. 26**) and **propane** (**Fig. 26B**). These differences in bond energy help to explain why **allylic** carbons are more prone to attack by chemically reactive species, which has major implications to the health of every cell in our body. For example <b><a class="one" href="https://opc-project.netlify.app/project/pnps/#Fig_VitCE" target="_blank" title="Go to PNP">polyunsaturated fatty acids</a></b> (**PUFA**), which is a major component of all cell membranes, are often damaged by **free radicals** because of their **bis-allylic** [[H]{#Blue}]{#strokeB} atoms (i.e. carbon atoms located between two double bonds). Fortunately we have **anti-oxidants** like **vitamin E** that can quench or neutralize **free radicals** before they can do any damage to the cell membranes. The overall changes in the [MO]{#Blk} energy of the **Allyl** system is perhaps best illustrated via an energy level diagram (**Fig. 27**). Clearly, according to [MOT]{#Blk}, combining a lone [2]{#Blk}[&pscr;<sub>z</sub>]{#Blue} orbital with an existing $\large \pi$-bonded <b>ethylene</b> molecule produces a lower energy **allyl** bonding [MO]{#Blk} and a higher energy anti-bonding [MO]{#Blk}. The longer <u>wavelength</u> of the bonding [MO]{#Blk} is clearly proportional to its lower energy state (i.e. $\text E \; = \; h \, \nu, \phantom{.} \text{where } \nu \propto 1/\lambda$).

For larger conjugated $\large \pi$-electron systems, like **1,3-butadiene**, its **Huckel** [MO]{#Blk} treatment involves the same steps described above for **ethylene** and **propylene**. Once the [MO]{#Blk} wave function is generated (**LCAO**) the **secular determinant** (i.e. 4 &times; 4 square matrix) can be calculated using the same recursive algebraic math.  


$$\\
\text{Let: } \large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize = \text{MO wave function}, \phantom{.} \large \phi \normalsize = 2p_z \; \text{wave funtion}, \phantom{.} c = \text{ coefficient}
\\
\large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1 \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; c_3 \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; + \; c_4 \large \phi_4
\\[15px]
\large \text{Matrix Form:}
\\
\text A \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \Big[ \; c_1, \; c_2, \; c_3, \; c_4 \; \Big] \phantom{.....} \text B \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \left[\begin{array}
\\
\large \phi_1 \\ \large \phi_2 \\ \large \phi_3 \\ \large \phi_4
\end{array}
\right]
\\
\large \psi_{\pi} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \text{A} \times \text{B} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \overbrace{ \Big[ \; c_1, \; c_2, \; c_3, \; c_4 \; \Big]
\left[\begin{array}
\\ \large \phi_1 \\ \large \phi_2 \\ \large \phi_3 \\ \large \phi_4
\end{array}
\right]}^{\large \text{Dot Product}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1 \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; c_2 \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; c_3 \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; + \; c_4 \large \phi_4
\\$$


$$\\
\begin{align*}
\overbrace{ \left| \begin{array}
\\
x & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} 0 & \phantom{.} 0
\\
1 & \phantom{.} x & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} 0
\\
0 & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} x & \phantom{.} 1
\\
0 & \phantom{.} 0 & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} x
\\
\end{array} \right| }^{\large |det|} \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} 0 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} x
\overbrace{ \left| \begin{array}
\\
x & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} 0
\\
1 & \phantom{.} x & \phantom{.} 1
\\
0 & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} x
\\
\end{array} \right|}^{\large \text M_{(1,1)}} \; - \; 1
\overbrace{ \left| \begin{array}
\\
1 & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} 0
\\
0 & \phantom{.} x & \phantom{.} 1
\\
0 & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} x
\\
\end{array} \right|}^{\large \text M^{'}_{(1,2)}} \normalsize \; + \; 0 \; - \; 0
\\
0 \phantom{.} = & \phantom{.} x \left[ x \overbrace{ \Bigg| \begin{array}
\\
x & \phantom{.} 1
\\
1 & \phantom{.} x
\\
\end{array} \Bigg| }^{\large \text M_{(1,1)}} \normalsize \; - \; 1 \overbrace{ \Bigg| \begin{array}
\\
1 & \phantom{.} 1
\\
0 & \phantom{.} x
\\
\end{array} \Bigg| }^{\large \text M_{(1,2)}} \normalsize \; + \; 0 \right] \; - \; 1 \left[ 1 \overbrace{ \Bigg| \begin{array}
\\
x & \phantom{.} 1
\\
1 & \phantom{.} x
\\
\end{array} \Bigg| }^{\large \text M^{'}_{(1,1)}} \normalsize \; - \; 1 \overbrace{ \Bigg| \begin{array}
\\
0 & \phantom{.} 1
\\
0 & \phantom{.} x
\\
\end{array} \Bigg| }^{\large \text M^{'}_{(1,2)}} \normalsize \; + \; 0 \right]
\\
0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} x \Bigg[ x \Big( x^2  \; - \; 1 \Big) \; - \; 1 \Big( x \; - \; 0 \Big) \Bigg] \; - \; 1 \Bigg[ 1 \Big( x^2 \; - \; 1 \Big) \; - \; 1 \Big( 0 \Big) \; + \; 0 \Bigg]
\\
0 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \bigg( x^4 \; - \; x^2 \; - \; x^2 \bigg) \; - \; \bigg( x^2 \; - \; 1 \bigg)
\\
0 \phantom{.} = & \phantom{.} x^4 \; - \; 3x^2 \; + \; 1
\\
\end{align*}$$


$$\large \text{Let:} \phantom{..} y = x^2
\\
y^2 \; - \; 3y \; + \; 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} \text{Use Quadratic Formula:} \quad \large x \normalsize \; = \; \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 \, - \, 4ac}}{2a}
\\
\large y \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{3 \; + \; \sqrt{9 \; - \; 4}}{2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 2.618 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} x^2 \phantom{.....} \large y \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{3 \; - \; \sqrt{9 \; - \; 4}}{2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0.382 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} x^2
\\
x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} - 1.618 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi_1}}{\beta} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_1} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; + \; 1.618 \, \beta
\\
x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} + 1.618 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi_4}}{\beta} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_4} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; - \; 1.618 \, \beta
\\
x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} - 0.618 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi_2}}{\beta} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_2} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; + \; 0.618 \, \beta
\\
x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} + 0.618 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \frac{\alpha \; - \; \text E_{\large \pi_3}}{\beta} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} \text E_{\large \pi_3} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \alpha \; - \; 0.618 \, \beta
\\$$


$$\\
\begin{array}
\\
  \left. \begin{matrix}
  \text E_{\large \pi_4} & \underline{\quad} & \phantom{.....} \alpha \; - \; 1.618 \, \beta
  \phantom{\Huge X}
  \\ \text E_{\large \pi_3} & \underline{\quad} & \alpha \; - \; 0.618 \, \beta
  \\ \text E_{\large \pi_2} & \underline{\uparrow \downarrow} & \alpha \; + \; 0.618 \, \beta
  \\ \text E_{\large \pi_1} & \underline{\uparrow \downarrow} & \alpha \; + \; 1.618 \, \beta &
  \\
  \end{matrix} \right\} &
  \begin{array}{l}
  \begin{align*} \large \text E_{\Large \pi \normalsize e^-} \normalsize \phantom{.} = & \phantom{.} 2(\alpha \; + \; 1.618 \, \beta) \; + \; 2(\alpha \; + \; 0.618 \, \beta) \\ = & \phantom{.} 4 \alpha \; + \; 4.472 \, \beta
  \\
  \end{align*}
  \end{array}
\end{array}
\\$$


$$\\
\large \text{De-localization Energy:}
\\
\Big[ \text{Note: De-localized versus Localized} \; 4 \pi e^- \; \text{Energy} \Big]
\\
\begin{align*}
\text E_{\text{(de-localized)}} \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} \large \text E_{\pi \normalsize \, (\text{1,3-butadiene})} \normalsize \; - \; \large \text E_{\pi \normalsize \, (2 \; \text{ethylenes})}
\\[4pt]
= & \phantom{.} \bigg[ 4 \alpha \; + \; 4.472 \, \beta \bigg] \; - \; \bigg[ 2 \Big(2 \alpha \; + \; 2 \, \beta \Big) \bigg]
\\
= & \phantom{.} \Big( \require{cancel} \cancel{4 \alpha} \; + \; 4.472 \, \beta \Big) \; - \; \Big( \require{cancel} \cancel{4 \alpha} \; + \; 4 \, \beta \Big) \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0.472 \, \beta
\\
\approx & \phantom{.} 90 \; \text{kJ/mole}
\\
\end{align*}$$


<hr style="border:1px solid gray">

$$\\
\large \text{Secular Equation & Coefficients in Matrix Form:}
\\
\overbrace{ \left|
\begin{array}
\\ \; x & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} 0 & \phantom{.} 0 \;
\\ \; 1 & \phantom{.} x & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} 0 \;
\\ \; 0 & \phantom{.} 1 & \phantom{.} x & \phantom{.} 1 \;

\end{array}
\right|}^{\large |det|} \phantom{..} \cdot 
\overbrace{ \left| \begin{array}
\\ \; c_1 \; \\ \; c_2 \; \\ \; c_3 \; \\ \; c_4 \;
\end{array} \right|}^{\large \text{coefficients}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{..} 0
\\$$


$$\\
\begin{align*}
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} & \phantom{..} c_1 \, x \; + \; c_2 \; + \; 0 \; + \; 0 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} c_1 \, x \; + \; c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} & \phantom{..} c_1 \; + \; c_2 \, x \; + \; c_3 \; + \; 0 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} c_1 \; + \; c_2 \, x \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{3} & \phantom{..} 0 \; + \; c_2 \; + \; c_3 \, x \; + \; c_4 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} c_2 \; + \; c_3 \, x \; + \; c_4 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} & \phantom{..} 0 \; + \; 0 \; + \; c_3 \; + \; c_4 \; x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} c_3 \; + \; c_4 \; x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0
\\
\end{align*}
\\ \;
\\
\large \text{Normalization Conditions}
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{\text N} \phantom{..} \large \sum_{i \, = \, 1}^{N} \normalsize c_i^2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1^2  \; + \; c_2^2 \; + \; c_3^2 \; + \; c_4^2
\\$$

$$\\

\\

\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} & \phantom{..} -1.618 \, c_1 \, x \; + \; c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} 1.618 \, c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_2
\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{2} & \phantom{..} c_1 \; - \; 1.618 \, c_2 \, x \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_1 \; + \; c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1.618 \, c_2
\\

\\
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{4} & \phantom{..} 0 \; + \; 0 \; + \; c_3 \; + \; c_4 \; x \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 0 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} 1.618 \, c_4 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_3
\\
\end{align*}$$


$$\\
\begin{align*}

\phantom{.} c_1 \; + \; c_3
\\

\phantom{.} c_1 \; + \; c_3

1.618 \, c_1 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_3
\\[5px]

\phantom{.} c_3 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} 1.618 \, c_1 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_4 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1

\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{7} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{1} \; + \; \require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{6} \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} 1.618 \, c_1 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{.} c_2 \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} c_2 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_3
\end{align*}
\\ \;
\\
\text{Express} \; \large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \; \text{coefficients in terms of} \; c_1
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} c_1 \, \Big[ \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; 1.618 \, \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; 1.618 \, \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; + \; \large \phi_4 \normalsize \Big]
\\$$


$$\large \text{Apply Normalization Conditions}
\\
\begin{align*}
\require{enclose} \enclose{circle}{\text N} \; \large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \phantom{..} \Longrightarrow \phantom{..} 1 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} c_1^2 \, (1)^2 \; + \; c_1^2 \, (1.618)^2 \; + \; c_1^2 \, (1.618)^2 \; + \; c_1^2 \, (1)^2
\\[5px]
1 \phantom{.} = &
\phantom{..} 7.236 \, c_1^2 \phantom{...} \Longrightarrow \phantom{...} c_1 \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{7.236}} \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} + 0.3717
\end{align*}
\\ \,
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \, 0.372 \, \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; (0.3717)(1.618) \, \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; (0.3717)(1.618) \, \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; + \; 0.3717 \, \large \phi_4
\\[15px]
\large \psi_{\pi_1} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \, 0.3717 \, \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; 0.6018 \, \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; 0.6018 \, \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; + \; 0.3717 \, \large \phi_4
\\[10px]
\Big[ \text{Bonding MO: all four} \; 2p_z \; \text{orbitals in phase} \Big]
\\$$


The same strategy shown above can be applied to the other $|det|$ roots (i.e. $x = \{ +1.618, +0.618, -0.618 \}$) in order to calculate the coefficients for the other higher energy [MO]{#Blk} (results shown below).  


$$\\
\large \psi_{\pi_2} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \, 0.6018 \, \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; + \; 0.3717 \, \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; - \; 0.3717 \, \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; - \; 0.6018 \, \large \phi_4
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_3} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \, 0.6018 \, \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; - \; 0.3717 \, \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; - \; 0.3717 \, \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; + \; 0.6018 \, \large \phi_4
\\
\large \psi_{\pi_4} \normalsize \phantom{.} = \phantom{.} \, 0.3717 \, \large \phi_1 \normalsize \; - \; 0.6018 \, \large \phi_2 \normalsize \; + \; 0.6018 \, \large \phi_3 \normalsize \; - \; 0.3717 \, \large \phi_4
\\$$
